name: Unique Layer Recovery in the Hall Three-Repair Assembly
statement: For the 1,203-concept terminal Hall assembly with three repair owners on layer coordinates $p,q$, one has $\mathcal B(X)=\{p,q\}$ and the only successful layer set is $\{p,q\}$. Starting the forced-enlargement procedure from either singleton forces the other coordinate and stops at the full pair, which recovers Hall's 299-concept seed and the three displayed repairs.
proof: Hall's shadow contains every support of size at most three. The three repairs add exactly their three four-coordinate supports, and no five-set has all its four-subsets among those additions. Hence the old minimal nonfaces are all four-sets except the three acquired supports; the mixed clauses replace precisely those three. Every old coordinate therefore occurs in 165 clauses, while each of $p,q$ occurs twice with opposite signs, giving the balanced set. If only $p$ is marked, the old part of the mixed clause owned by the positive-$p$ repair has two solutions in the recovery family, so its fibre is not a singleton; marking only $q$ fails symmetrically. Marking both coordinates gives three distinct singleton fibres, recovers Hall, and verifies success. These same collisions force the missing coordinate in each singleton-start closure.
comments: The fixed regression enumerates every candidate layer subset, checks both failed singleton recoveries and the full-pair recovery, and confirms the corresponding thick-coordinate, owner-count, and resolving-addition branch of the layer-recovery dichotomy.
